current_formulation: Boumans et al. link articles to agency copy by cosine similarity and score verbatim reuse with a churnalism index.

steps.formulation: METER sorts newspaper stories into wholly derived, partially derived, and non-derived from agency copy, by journalists' judgement.
steps.quote: wholly-derived (WD): all text in the newspaper article is rewritten only from news agency copy

criticism.quote: Although the corpus can be used to evaluate plagiarism detection its design does not support this task.

steps.formulation: PAN-PC-10 models reuse as a source passage under artificial or human obfuscation.
steps.quote: Since verbatim copies can be detected easily, plagiarists often rewrite ssrc to obfuscate their illegitimate act.

steps.formulation: Agency dependence is measured by text comparison: a cosine link, then a churnalism index for verbatim reuse.
steps.quote: when the churnalism index > .7, the two texts are nearly identical

criticism.quote: the agency and the newspaper independently of each other replicate the same source text, such as a press release.
